default.what: Penetration (distance travelled before solvation) of a sub-excitation electron: a 3D Gaussian whose mean radius is a 12th-degree polynomial fit in the electron energy. Used when /process/dna/e-SolvationSubType is not given (G4EmLowEParameters default fMeesungnoen2002eSolvation).

alternatives.what: Mean radius r_mean = 1.8 nm per eV of electron energy, then a 3D Gaussian with the same conversion as Meesungnoen2002.
Same model as the default, written explicitly.
3D standard deviation interpolated from a table of energies 0.2 to 9 eV (Terrisol and Beaudre 1990); an energy above 9 eV is a fatal error in this model.

displacement.what: Gives each pre-chemical product its starting offset from the ionised or excited water molecule. Each offset is a 3D Gaussian: the number below is the RMS radius Rrms, the per-axis sigma being Rrms/sqrt(3). The solvated electron of an auto-ionisation channel uses the solvation model instead. The displacement type of each channel is set in G4ChemDissociationChannels_option1, which the project uses.

rows.what: One of the two products, chosen with probability 1/2, stays at the origin; the other is displaced.
Same choice as ionisation: one product at the origin, the other displaced; the solvated electron e_aq is placed by the solvation model.
One displacement vector shared by the pair: OH gets -1/18 of it, H gets +17/18.

rows.case: B1A1_DissociationDecay and DissociativeAttachment: H2 + 2 OH (shared vector)
rows.what: H2 gets -16/18 of the shared vector, each OH gets +2/18 of it plus its own offset (below).

rows.case: B1A1_DissociationDecay and DissociativeAttachment: OH own offset
rows.what: Added to the shared-vector part; the two OH take +0.5 and -0.5 of one sampled offset.
O stays at the origin; the two H take +0.5 and -0.5 of one sampled offset.

rows.case: Double, triple and quadruple ionisation channels: H3O+ (and the other products not listed below)
rows.what: Radius used for every H3O+ except the extra ones noted next; O(3P) stays at the origin (radius 0).

rows.case: Double, triple and quadruple ionisation channels: OH and the extra H3O+
rows.what: The OH uses this radius; the extra H3O+ (second in DoubleIonisation_DissociationDecay1, second in Decay2, third and fourth in the triple and quadruple cases) uses it too and, where an OH is present, is also shifted by that OH's offset.

meso.partialPairs: Reaction type 1 (partially diffusion-controlled) does not change the Gillespie propensity: G4DNAGillespieDirectMethod::PropensityFunction uses GetObservedReactionRateConstant() divided by Avogadro times the voxel volume, and G4DNAMolecularReactionData::SetReactionType(1) leaves that observed rate unchanged (it sets the reaction radius, effective radius, diffusion and activation rates and probability). The one place type 1 can matter in the mesoscopic stage is the mesh-resolution check, which reads GetEffectiveReactionRadius.

physical.text: Physical stage: the electron or proton track is followed with the physics processes above. The simulation time attributed to it is not stated in the sources checked; the chemistry stage starts at 1 ps.

prechem.text: Pre-chemical stage: each ionised, excited or attached water molecule is created as a molecule track at global time 1 ps (plus the pulse delay, 0 here); the solvated electron is also created at 1 ps. The water molecule's decay time is 0, so its dissociation channel fires at that same time and the products take the track's global time. The end of the stage is not a fixed number in the sources.

hetero.text: Particle-based stage (IRT_syn or SBS): from the 1 ps start to the hand-over time when the mesoscopic stage is on (default 5 ns), otherwise to the end time (default 1 us without the mesoscopic stage).

meso.text: Mesoscopic stage (IRT_syn only): from the hand-over time (default 5 ns) to the end time (default 1 s with the mesoscopic stage).
